labelPolicy: 3 directly answers; 2 relevant to deliberately ambiguous symptom; archived sources relevant only to historical questions

documents.title: PostgreSQL connection exhaustion — current
documents.text:
# PostgreSQL connection exhaustion

Checkout HTTP 503 came from leaked JDBC connections. HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms. pg_stat_activity showed idle in transaction. Close connections with try-with-resources, cancel abandoned transactions, then set the pool maximum to 20. Restarting PostgreSQL is not the first action.

documents.title: PostgreSQL connection exhaustion — similar
documents.text:
# PostgreSQL connection exhaustion

Checkout HTTP 503 also occurred during a database lock convoy. The pool had free connections; pg_locks showed a schema migration holding AccessExclusiveLock. Stop the blocking migration after approval. Increasing maximumPoolSize cannot fix a lock convoy.

documents.title: PostgreSQL connection exhaustion — archived
documents.text:
# PostgreSQL connection exhaustion

Archived 2022 database recovery: pool maximum 80 and service restart were used on a smaller single-instance system. This procedure is obsolete after the JDBC leak fix. Do not apply its pool setting to current checkout.

documents.title: Authentication and authorization failures — current
documents.text:
# Authentication and authorization failures

AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED is HTTP 401: renew the access token using the approved login flow. Validate signature, issuer and traceback-api audience. An MCP-only resource token cannot authenticate REST. Never log bearer tokens while diagnosing a failed login.

documents.title: Authentication and authorization failures — similar
documents.text:
# Authentication and authorization failures

ORG_MEMBERSHIP_REMOVED is HTTP 403 despite a valid unexpired token. Read current persisted memberships; token roles and email are not organization authority. Restore membership only through an administrator's approved workflow. Token refresh does not recreate membership.

documents.title: Authentication and authorization failures — archived
documents.text:
# Authentication and authorization failures

Archived gateway v1 reported all authorization failures as HTTP 500. It accepted audience legacy-api. Current resource servers require traceback-api and distinguish 401 authentication from 403 membership. This gateway guide is retained solely for historical incident analysis.

documents.title: HTTP 500 502 and 503 at the gateway — current
documents.text:
# HTTP 500 502 and 503 at the gateway

Payments gateway HTTP 502 with upstream prematurely closed connection was caused by backend pod termination. Compare upstream reset counters and pod termination timestamps. Drain traffic before shutdown and set terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 45. This is different from an application HTTP 500.

documents.title: HTTP 500 502 and 503 at the gateway — similar
documents.text:
# HTTP 500 502 and 503 at the gateway

Payments HTTP 500 stack trace: java.lang.NullPointerException at InvoiceMapper.map(InvoiceMapper.java:87). No upstream reset occurred. Roll back invoice mapper release r42. HTTP 503 with Retry-After instead means deliberate admission rejection; retries must be bounded.

documents.title: HTTP 500 502 and 503 at the gateway — archived
documents.text:
# HTTP 500 502 and 503 at the gateway

Archived edge proxy config treated every 502 as DNS failure and advised flushing DNS immediately. The old proxy emitted no upstream reset metric. Current runbooks require distinguishing backend termination, mapper exceptions and admission 503 before changing network settings.

documents.title: Kubernetes deployment failures — current
documents.text:
# Kubernetes deployment failures

Deployment checkout-v3 stalled with ProgressDeadlineExceeded. A readiness path changed from /ready to /health/ready while the probe still used the old path. Verify endpoints and rollout status, patch the probe, and resume only when ready replicas stabilize. Do not disable readiness checks.

documents.title: Kubernetes deployment failures — similar
documents.text:
# Kubernetes deployment failures

The same checkout deployment stalled with ImagePullBackOff because registry credentials expired. Pod events showed failed to authorize pulling image. Renew the imagePullSecret through the approved secret workflow, then retry rollout. Changing readiness paths does not fix image pulls.

documents.title: Kubernetes deployment failures — archived
documents.text:
# Kubernetes deployment failures

Archived Kubernetes rollout guide used maxUnavailable=100% and disabled readiness during deployment. It predates zero-downtime checkout. Keep it for historical context; current rollout uses maxUnavailable=0 and tested readiness probes.

documents.title: JVM memory growth — current
documents.text:
# JVM memory growth

java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space in report generation followed an unbounded tenantReportCache. Retained byte arrays dominated the heap histogram. Bound cache entries by weight, close report streams and compare retained heap after garbage collection. Capture only synthetic or sanitized heap evidence.

documents.title: JVM memory growth — similar
documents.text:
# JVM memory growth

A report worker was OOMKilled with stable Java heap. Native direct buffers grew while Netty pooled allocations remained unreleased. Track process RSS versus heap and release ByteBuf ownership exactly once. Increasing Java Xmx may worsen this container native-memory incident.

documents.title: JVM memory growth — archived
documents.text:
# JVM memory growth

Archived report memory guide set -Xmx equal to the container memory limit. It omitted native buffers and JVM overhead. The setting is obsolete; historical heap charts alone cannot diagnose RSS-driven OOMKilled events.

documents.title: Safe rollback procedures — current
documents.text:
# Safe rollback procedures

Release ledger-r18 rollback order: 1. Pause new writes. 2. Verify schema compatibility with ledger-r17. 3. Switch traffic to r17. 4. Resume writes after smoke checks. The additive nullable column is backward compatible. Preserve source rows and audit records.

documents.title: Safe rollback procedures — similar
documents.text:
# Safe rollback procedures

Ledger-r19 introduced a destructive currency type migration. Application rollback alone is unsafe because r17 cannot read the new representation. Stop writes and escalate to the database recovery owner; use the reviewed forward repair. Do not run an automatic down migration.

documents.title: Safe rollback procedures — archived
documents.text:
# Safe rollback procedures

Archived ledger emergency guide restored last night's database snapshot on every failed deploy. This loses later writes and is superseded. It is relevant only to analysis of the 2021 rollback incident, not current recovery instructions.

documents.title: Network timeout diagnosis — current
documents.text:
# Network timeout diagnosis

Partner API requests failed with java.net.SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out after 2000ms. TCP connect completed quickly, but the peer stalled response bodies. Set a bounded read deadline and retry only idempotent requests with jitter. Trace connect and first-byte durations separately.

documents.title: Network timeout diagnosis — similar
documents.text:
# Network timeout diagnosis

Partner integration failed with java.net.UnknownHostException: partner.internal. Resolver NXDOMAIN preceded any TCP connection. Inspect service discovery and DNS records; changing the response read timeout cannot fix name resolution. Avoid retry storms during DNS recovery.

documents.title: Network timeout diagnosis — archived
documents.text:
# Network timeout diagnosis

Archived partner client disabled all connect and read timeouts to tolerate slow responses. Calls then occupied the whole connection pool. The guide is obsolete; current clients have separate finite connect and read deadlines.

documents.title: Distributed job leases — current
documents.text:
# Distributed job leases

Export job JOB_LEASE_LOST occurs after worker restart and replacement claim. Persist a unique lease token, renew before expiry, and compare that token during finalization. A stale worker may finish computation but cannot commit results. Redelivery is expected; result publication must be idempotent.

documents.title: Distributed job leases — similar
documents.text:
# Distributed job leases

Export jobs remained PENDING because the outbox dispatcher crashed after database commit but before queue send. Reconcile undelivered outbox rows and resume bounded dispatch. There was no worker lease to renew yet; changing worker timeouts cannot publish missing messages.

documents.title: Distributed job leases — archived
documents.text:
# Distributed job leases

Archived export worker used a process-local boolean as its only lock. Multiple hosts executed duplicate side effects after restart. It predates durable token fencing and must not be reused for current distributed jobs.

documents.title: Cache invalidation and permissions — current
documents.text:
# Cache invalidation and permissions

Profile reads showed old display names after a database update because profile_cache:v2 invalidation was omitted. Publish invalidation after successful commit and bound entry lifetime. Use the organization in every cache key. This data cache must never become authorization authority.

documents.title: Cache invalidation and permissions — similar
documents.text:
# Cache invalidation and permissions

A permissions prototype cached organization membership in a process-local map and served stale authorization after revocation. Remove that authorization cache and query current membership. A profile display-cache TTL change cannot enforce immediate membership removal.

documents.title: Cache invalidation and permissions — archived
documents.text:
# Cache invalidation and permissions

Archived profile guide flushed the entire shared cache on each update and keyed entries only by numeric user ID. It predates tenant keys. Retain for incident reconstruction; current cache keys include organization identity.

documents.title: API rate limiting — current
documents.text:
# API rate limiting

Public API returns HTTP 429 RATE_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED with Retry-After. Partition budgets by authorized organization and client identity, cap map growth, and apply jittered bounded retries. A caller must not select another tenant's bucket through a request field.

documents.title: API rate limiting — similar
documents.text:
# API rate limiting

The same client saw HTTP 503 GENERATION_CAPACITY when all local inference slots were busy. This is concurrent admission, not a one-minute rate budget. Do not spawn unbounded retry threads; wait for occupied calls to finish before retrying with the same operation key.

documents.title: API rate limiting — archived
documents.text:
# API rate limiting

Archived API limiter kept every anonymous client-supplied key forever and omitted Retry-After. A later bounded fixed-window implementation replaced it. The old process-local limiter never provided a global distributed quota.

documents.title: Queue retries and dead letters — current
documents.text:
# Queue retries and dead letters

Ingestion QUEUE_UNAVAILABLE leaves the transactional outbox pending. Dispatch retries with exponential backoff. A send followed by delivery-commit failure can duplicate messages, so consumers compare persisted job identity and complete idempotently. Never delete a committed event to clear backlog.

documents.title: Queue retries and dead letters — similar
documents.text:
# Queue retries and dead letters

Poison ingestion payload INVALID_MESSAGE reached the dead-letter queue after eight receives. Inspect sanitized event identifiers, repair the producer, and redrive only eligible messages. Redriving does not reset a terminal FAILED job; an approved new-generation retry is separate.

documents.title: Queue retries and dead letters — archived
documents.text:
# Queue retries and dead letters

Archived ingestion retry guide acknowledged every failed message before persisting failure. Lost work followed. Current consumers acknowledge only durable successful or obsolete handling and leave recoverable failures for redelivery.

documents.title: Observability and alerting — current
documents.text:
# Observability and alerting

Alert OUTBOX_AGE_HIGH measures oldest pending publication age, not just event count. Correlate queue reachability, failed publication counters and worker lease age. Labels contain only fixed states/outcomes; never raw organization UUIDs, document text, tokens or user questions.

documents.title: Observability and alerting — similar
documents.text:
# Observability and alerting

Alert API_ERROR_BURN tracks the ratio of HTTP 5xx to total requests over short and long windows. A low-volume endpoint can have high percentage with few requests, so inspect volume and latency together. Health liveness must not include remote inference dependency failure.

documents.title: Observability and alerting — archived
documents.text:
# Observability and alerting

Archived monitoring guide labeled each timer with raw request URLs and access-token subject. This caused unbounded cardinality and privacy exposure. Current metrics use route templates and fixed outcomes; the old dashboards are obsolete.

documents.title: Production incident postmortems — current
documents.text:
# Production incident postmortems

Synthetic incident INC-204: invoice HTTP 503 lasted 17 minutes after a release doubled concurrent database borrowers. No data loss occurred. Mitigation reduced pool demand and rolled back the new fan-out. Follow-up adds load tests and an alert on pending borrowers; owner is the platform team.

documents.title: Production incident postmortems — similar
documents.text:
# Production incident postmortems

Synthetic incident INC-205: invoice HTTP 503 lasted 11 minutes during a network policy rollout. Database capacity stayed normal; denied egress caused socket connect timeouts. Revert the network policy and test connectivity. Pool expansion was not the corrective action.

documents.title: Production incident postmortems — archived
documents.text:
# Production incident postmortems

Archived INC-104 postmortem attributed invoice 503 to database saturation without checking network policy. Its root-cause statement was later withdrawn. Use INC-204 and INC-205 for current differentiated evidence rather than treating the shared symptom as proof.
